question_type: least-squares quadratic projection of four monthly capital-movement totals, divided by an external-knowledge day number

opus_path.decision: 'Aggregate international flows of liquid banking funds (excluding brokerage balances and security transactions)' = the 'MOVEMENT IN SHORT-TERM BANKING FUNDS' section of 'Net Capital Movement between the United States and Foreign Countries' (the other sections are brokerage balances and domestic/foreign securities); 'monthly grand total' = the 'Grand total' column of the 'Total <Month>' row, in $ thousands.

Each month's total from the 1939 issue that prints that month: Aug issue (May), Sep (June), Oct (July), Nov (August). Checked later 1939-1940 issues: each prints only its latest month plus cumulative rows, so there are no revised printings.
Took the printed 'Total <Month>' Grand total cell (last numeric cell on the line) and re-read each line in the script with an assertion.

Cross-checked each monthly total against the sum of its weekly rows and against differences of the cumulative rows. For May the weekly rows did not add up because one weekly cell is OCR-garbled; the printed total agreed with the cumulative difference, so the total row was kept.

Least-squares quadratic on t=1..4 (np.polyfit) projected to t=5, cross-checked with exact rational normal equations (Fractions + Gaussian elimination); the reviewer also used the closed-form 4-point LS extrapolation weights.
External knowledge: invasion day number in September 1939 (divide by it).
The unrounded result sits exactly on a .5 boundary; checked that half-up and half-even give the same integer.

opus_key_moves: Treated 'fit a quadratic regression to four points' as an overdetermined least-squares fit and computed it in a script, with an exact-arithmetic cross-check.
Verified each monthly total against weekly sums and cumulative-row differences, which caught an OCR-garbled weekly cell without letting it change the total.

It submitted the hand result at [39] without running any script; the submitted number never appears in any tool output.
first_divergence.what_opus_did: Least-squares quadratic via np.polyfit plus exact normal equations in Fractions (calc.py:26-53).

text_vs_mechanism: A text rule would plausibly fix this, since the same model fixed it unprompted in two of three arms and the later cards deck carries the right text (C019). A mechanism is more reliable because the error is silent and confident: an answer-provenance CHECK or a working numeric TOOL would have prevented it deterministically.
notes: Rounding is fragile here (the least-squares projection lands on .5 before rounding), so a correct method with a different rounding convention could still fail; Opus checked both half-up and half-even. Harness friction (no heredoc, no numpy, fragile python -c quoting) is the upstream cause of the method substitution. Fixing the sandbox or documenting the working write-a-script path removes a whole class of 'compute by hand' errors.
